title: To amend title 5, United States Code, to authorize the increase of the retirement age in the United States Capitol Police.

claims.claim: Capitol Police officers currently face mandatory retirement at age 60
claims.sourceSpan: striking becomes 60 years of age
claims.note: 60 is verbatim as the struck (pre-amendment) age. Exact word 'mandatory' is not in the excerpt, but the bill title frames it as 'the retirement age' and the amended clause is a fixed separation age — a defensible reading.

claims.claim: This bill replaces that fixed age with a range, letting the Board set the mandatory retirement age at any point between 57 and 65
claims.sourceSpan: attains an age determined by the Board that shall be not less than 57 years of age and not more than 65 years of age

claims.claim: the Capitol Police Board
claims.sourceSpan: an age determined by the Board
claims.note: Source says only 'the Board'; in a bill titled 'United States Capitol Police' amending the Capitol Police retirement provisions, 'the Board' resolves to the Capitol Police Board. Exact name not verbatim in this excerpt.

claims.claim: giving it more flexibility to retain experienced officers beyond the current 60-year cap
claims.sourceSpan: authorize the increase of the retirement age in the United States Capitol Police
claims.note: Upward/retention framing tracks the bill's official title ('the increase of the retirement age'). Note: the new range floor of 57 also permits a mandatory age BELOW the current 60, which this clause does not surface (disclosed elsewhere via the range).

claims.claim: Raises the Capitol Police Board's maximum retirement age from 60 to 65
claims.sourceSpan: attains an age determined by the Board that shall be not less than 57 years of age and not more than 65 years of age
claims.note: New maximum 65 verbatim; prior 60 via 'striking becomes 60 years of age'.

claims.claim: maximum retirement age waiver
claims.sourceSpan: an age determined by the Board
claims.note: The word 'waiver' appears nowhere in the source. The bill changes the mandatory-retirement trigger from a fixed 60 to a Board-DETERMINED age (57-65); it does not raise a 'waiver' ceiling. 'waiver' is an extrinsic mechanism gloss. Net effect (officers may serve to 65) is correctly stated.

claims.claim: Section 8335(c) of title 5, United States Code (CSRS) — Capitol Police mandatory retirement age ceiling raised from 60 to 65, at the Board's discretion
claims.sourceSpan: Civil Service Retirement System Section 8335(c) of title 5, United States Code, is amended by striking becomes 60 years of age and inserting attains an age determined by the Board that shall be not less than 57 years of age and not more than 65 years of age
claims.note: 8335(c)=CSRS; ceiling 60->65 at Board discretion all sourced. 'ceiling raised' captures the new maximum but omits that the new floor (57) is below the prior fixed 60.

claims.claim: Section 8425(c) of title 5, United States Code (FERS) — Capitol Police mandatory retirement age ceiling raised from 60 to 65, at the Board's discretion
claims.sourceSpan: Section 8425(c) of title 5, United States Code, is amended by striking becomes 60 years of age and inserting attains an age determined by the Board that shall be not less than 57 years of age and not more than 65 years of age
claims.note: 8425(c)=FERS; identical amendment to the CSRS provision.

claims.claim: OMISSION: the new range's floor of 57 permits a mandatory retirement age BELOW the current 60 (the Board could lower it), not only raise it
claims.sourceSpan: not less than 57 years of age
claims.note: The analysis consistently frames the change as an increase ('ceiling raised from 60 to 65', 'keep officers working longer', 'beyond the current 60-year cap'). Because the Board may set any age >=57, it could also set a mandatory age below the current 60. This downward possibility is disclosed via the range floor (57) in summary/top_lines/gaps but is never stated as a direction of change. Minor: fully disclosed as a range, and the bill's own title frames it as 'the increase of the retirement age'.

notes: Source = introduced House text (IH), 1533 chars, one operative section, no referencedSources registered. versionChanges.unchanged=true through the Engrossed (EH) version, so the IH text governs the analysis. Zero material findings: all figures (57, 60, 65), statutory cites (8335(c), 8425(c), title 5), retirement systems (CSRS/FERS), sponsors (Steil, Morelle), and direction-of-change (expand Board authority / raise max) verify verbatim against source. Minor imprecisions: (1) brief calls the mechanism a 'waiver' — the word is absent from source; the bill changes a Board-DETERMINED age, not a waiver ceiling (net 60->65 effect still correct); (2) the change is framed only as an increase, but the range floor of 57 also permits a mandatory age below the current 60 (disclosed via the range, and the bill title itself says 'increase'); (3) 'for individual officers or as a general/department-wide policy' is an interpretive reading of the ambiguous 'an age determined by the Board'; (4) likelihoodReason party labels (R-WI/D-NY) and the 'typically advances with little controversy' / Senate-passage predictions are cache-metadata/editorial, not in bill text.
